approach: Read acceleration from the slope of each v-t segment, and get position by adding the signed area under v-t to the given starting position.

steps.text: Find the slope of the v-t line at t = 1 s, 3 s and 9 s from the segment each falls in.
steps.equation: a(1 s) = 5 m/s² (0–2 s segment), a(3 s) = 0 (2–4 s segment, constant v), a(9 s) = 5 m/s² (8–10 s segment)

steps.text: Start the position at s = 10 m at t = 0 and add the area under v-t up to each breakpoint to find s at t = 10 s.
For 0 ≤ t ≤ 2 s, v = 5t; integrate to get s(t).
For 4 s ≤ t ≤ 8 s, v = 10 − 5(t − 4), starting from s(4) = 40 m; integrate and collect terms in t.

common_mistakes.text: Reading the acceleration at t = 3 s as nonzero, forgetting that a straight horizontal segment of the v-t graph means zero acceleration.
Writing the s-t equation for 4 s ≤ t ≤ 8 s starting the position from zero instead of from s(4) = 40 m, the value already reached by that time.
